content: The dosage of chloroquine phosphate is typically expressed in terms of its equivalent chloroquine base. Each 250 mg tablet of chloroquine phosphate corresponds to 150 mg of chloroquine base, and each 500 mg tablet corresponds to 300 mg of chloroquine base. For infants and children, the dosage is preferably calculated based on body weight. Malaria Suppression Adult Dose: 500 mg (equivalent to 300 mg base) taken on the same day each week. Pediatric Dose: The weekly suppressive dose is 5 mg of base per kilogram of body weight, not exceeding the adult dose regardless of weight. Suppressive therapy should ideally begin two weeks prior to exposure. If this is not feasible, adults may take an initial double (loading) dose of 1 g (600 mg base), and children may take 10 mg base per kilogram, divided into two doses taken six hours apart. Suppressive therapy should continue for eight weeks after leaving the endemic area. Treatment of Acute Malaria Attack Adult Regimen: An initial dose of 1 g (600 mg base), followed by an additional 500 mg (300 mg base) six to eight hours later, and then 500 mg (300 mg base) once daily for the next two consecutive days. This totals 1.5 g base over three days. Pediatric Regimen: First dose: 10 mg base per kilogram (not exceeding 600 mg base in a single dose). Second dose (6 hours after the first): 5 mg base per kilogram (not exceeding 300 mg base in a single dose). Third dose (24 hours after the first): 5 mg base per kilogram. Fourth dose (36 hours after the first): 5 mg base per kilogram. For radical cure of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium malariae infections, concomitant therapy with an 8-aminoquinoline compound is required. Extraintestinal Amebiasis Adults: 1 g (600 mg base) daily for two days, followed by 500 mg (300 mg base) daily for at least two to three weeks. Treatment is usually combined with an effective intestinal amebicide. Geriatric Use Refer to the Precautions section under Geriatric Use for specific considerations.
